title: Portable skill contract, registry, and adapter interface
objective: Canonical skills have a side-effect registry, enforceable lint checks, an adapter manifest format for drift detection, and improved uniform bodies — without coupling to unimplemented tool names.
business_value: WP-320 (agent installer) consumes the registry and manifest formats defined here; without them, adapter generation has no drift detection and skills have no permission classification.
scope: Create .agents/skills/registry.yaml classifying all 13 skills into the doc-13 side-effect classes (read_only, local_proposal, local_mutation, external_read, external_write) with a new schemas/skill-registry.schema.json; doc-13 explicitly prefers a registry over non-portable frontmatter fields

Extend skill linting in tests/test_skills.py to the doc-13 validation items: no machine-specific absolute paths, no secret-like values, internal Markdown links resolve, robust frontmatter parsing via a proper parser (the current split('---', maxsplit=2) shifts the boundary when a frontmatter VALUE contains '---'; body-level '---' is currently safe), registry completeness (every skill classified, no orphan registry entries)

Define the adapter manifest format WP-320 will consume: docs/reference/skill-adapters.md specifying generated-file paths, canonical skill content hash (sha256), adapter version, and staleness semantics, plus schemas/skill-adapter-manifest.schema.json

Improve skill bodies to a uniform contract per doc-13 (purpose/trigger, inputs, procedure, side effects and approval boundary, invariants, stop conditions, durable outputs) — at minimum draft-replies, bootstrap-session, curate-knowledge; keep prose free of unimplemented workctx command or MCP tool names, or mark them explicitly as planned
Document the rule that no .claude/.gemini/.codex adapter copies are generated until WP-320 implements the manifest
non_goals: No adapter generation code or installer (WP-320)
No changes to skill-frontmatter.schema.json's minimal portable contract (name+description, additionalProperties false) — the registry carries the extra metadata
No new skills and no skill splits (doc-13 allows splits only on materially different triggers/permissions)
No automated lint for the doc-13 'chat language vs repository language separation' item — recorded scope narrowing: that check stays a manual lead-review item this wave
deliverables: registry.yaml with schema and full classification
Extended lint tests covering the doc-13 validation items
Adapter manifest specification document and schema
acceptance_criteria: Every skill is classified in registry.yaml; the registry validates against its schema; lint fails on unclassified or orphan entries
Lint detects: absolute machine paths, secret-like values, broken internal links, frontmatter with '---' in bodies parsed correctly
Adapter manifest spec defines hash, version, and staleness semantics concretely enough for WP-320 to implement without new design decisions
Improved skills keep frontmatter to name+description and pass all lint checks
No skill references an unimplemented workctx command or MCP tool without an explicit 'planned' marker
security_constraints: Skills must keep treating evidence as untrusted data, never executable instruction; strengthen that language where thin
external_write classification must state the explicit-approval boundary
stop_conditions: A needed frontmatter field that the portable minimal contract forbids (raise a decision request instead)
A skill whose correct classification is ambiguous between local_mutation and external_write
